## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `action-legality-conditioned-assembly`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-29T16:59:47.781Z.

Entry slug action-legality-conditioned-assembly.

The gap. Every scoring signal in the engine ranks items - what is relevant, recent, blocking, close to an outcome, likely to be touched. Nothing in the assembly says what the reader may legally do next. An agent receives a bounded set of items and must then discover, one failed mutation at a time, which transitions those items admit. Measured this session: the workspace schema declares six role-to-status aliases and no transition relation at all, so a closed item accepts a move to in_progress or even to draft with no warning, and there is no machine-readable source from which the legal action set for an item in a state could be read.

The mechanism. Condition the assembly on the action space, not only the item space. For each candidate, carry the set of transitions and mutations that are legal for the reading identity given the item's current state, and let that set participate in scoring: an item whose only legal action is to wait is worth fewer tokens than one that can be started now, even at equal relevance. Two consequences follow. A context assembly becomes a policy input rather than a reading list, which is what an evaluation episode or a reinforcement-learning policy needs. And the omission cost changes shape - withholding an item the reader cannot act on is cheap, withholding the one item they could have started is the expensive mistake.

Degeneracy requirement. When the transition relation is total and unrestricted - every action legal for every item, which is the product's behaviour today - every candidate carries an identical action set, the term contributes a constant, and ranking must be bit-identical to the current engine. That is the acceptance test, and it is why this entry cannot land before a declared transition relation exists.

Prerequisites and owners. The declarative policy engine owns the transition relation as data. The episode substrate is the first consumer that needs the action set to be observable. The relevance contract and the token-budget packer own the scoring surface this term plugs into.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
